title: Run two coding agents side by side and set firm rules
summary: A developer ran Codex and Claude Code on two projects for weeks; he reports Claude Code delivered 9 usable features in a day while Codex stalled on permission requests.
agent_role: Both agents ran groups of helper agents to build features, some overnight; the author wrote rule sheets, reviewed results and pushed stalled work forward.
outcome: Author reports Claude Code shipped 9 times in a day while Codex stopped 3 times and built for about 18 minutes.
what_they_did: The poster ran Codex and Claude Code side by side for weeks on two real projects. He gave each a one-page rule sheet and left Claude Code running two teams overnight. He then wrote nine rules for running any agent.
how_it_went: He says Claude Code produced three usable things overnight and nine by mid-afternoon. Codex stalled, even asking permission to remove its own self-written rules.
worth_knowing: He says both agents waste effort on status reports and self-reviews, and that rules matter more than which tool you pick.
prompt: You are working on [project]. Follow these rules: done means I can open it and see it working. Only I write rules; if you invent one, delete it. When you explain a problem, fix it right away. Make one round of changes, then stop for my review. Keep reports to ten lines. Do not wait on me overnight; keep building on [task list]. Never make final decisions, deploy or delete anything without asking me first.

curation.rationale: A real side-by-side account of running two coding agents on projects, with specific counts and practical rules, though the projects themselves are vague.
